title: Medical Office Replacement Property Sourcing
name: Medical Office Replacement Property Sourcing
metaTitle: Medical Office Replacement Property Sourcing in San Diego, CA
metaDescription: Medical office replacement sourcing in San Diego checked the way a bid should be checked: tenant improvement exposure, suite specialty, and lease structure first.

sections.html: A medical office quote that lists square footage and an asking cap rate and stops there is skipping the two figures that actually decide whether the building works as a replacement: what it costs to re-lease a vacated suite, and how much of the rent roll depends on one health system's renewal decision. San Diego's medical office stock is thin enough that a listing can look fully priced on paper and still carry re-leasing risk underneath it.

sections.heading: What a Medical Office Bid Usually Leaves Off the Page
sections.html:
Ask for these five items before a San Diego medical office candidate goes on your identification list. If the sourcing quote you were handed doesn't already include them, that's the tell that the number you were given is a starting point, not a real price.

  • Trailing tenant-improvement allowance and remaining amortization on every suite, not only the anchor tenant
  • Whether the build-out is specialty-specific — imaging, surgical, dental — versus a general shell that re-leases to any practice
  • Plumbing, gas line, and electrical capacity rated for the next tenant's use, not only the current one
  • Parking ratio required for medical occupancy against what the site actually provides
  • Certificate-of-occupancy status and any open life-safety corrections

sections.heading: Torrey Pines and UTC Are Pulling Space Out of the Medical Office Pool
sections.html:
Life-science tenants around Torrey Pines and UTC have been converting standard office floor plates to lab-capable space for years, and that competition reaches into medical office pricing because the same buildings, and often the same landlords, are weighing a lab conversion against a straight medical office lease. A vacant suite near that corridor can be priced as if a lab tenant will take it, which is a different bet than pricing it for a family practice or urgent-care operator.

Before treating that upside as underwriting, confirm the shell's ceiling height, floor loading, and mechanical capacity actually support a lab build-out. A building priced for lab conversion that can't structurally support one is a mispriced medical office, not a discounted lab building.

sections.heading: Reading a Health System Lease Like the Renewal Is Already in Question
sections.html:
Scripps, Sharp, and UC San Diego Health all lease space off their owned campuses in addition to occupying it, and each system's own real estate strategy — consolidating outpatient services onto owned land, for instance — can shorten the practical life of a lease well before its stated term ends. A full-service lease with a below-market base rent looks attractive until you check whether the tenant has an early-termination right tied to system consolidation.

Net leases in this asset class shift operating costs to the tenant but rarely shift the risk that a specialty build-out sits vacant longer than a general-practice shell would. Price that vacancy risk explicitly rather than folding it into a flat cap rate.

sections.heading: Matching the 45-Day List to a Market That Doesn't Turn Over Fast
sections.html: Medical office listings in San Diego don't cycle the way multifamily or retail does, so waiting until day thirty of the identification window to start building a short list is how exchangers end up naming a property they haven't actually underwritten. Start the search on day one of the relinquished-property closing, not after it, so the qualified intermediary has real candidates to work with rather than whatever is left on the market by day forty.

sections.heading: Getting the Qualified Intermediary and Lender Talking Early
sections.html: Lenders underwriting medical office debt in San Diego want to see the specialty mix and lease-renewal timeline before they'll commit to terms, and that review can take longer than a standard office loan. Loop the qualified intermediary in on the timeline so funds are staged correctly against the 180-day exchange period, and treat any gap between the debt you retire and the debt you place as a boot question to raise with a tax advisor before closing, not after.

faqs.q: What due diligence is different on a medical office building compared to standard office?
faqs.a: Medical suites carry specialty-specific build-outs, higher parking ratios, and plumbing or gas capacity that a general office tenant never needs, so re-leasing cost and time run higher than a standard office comparable. Confirm the current tenant improvement amortization and specialty classification before assuming the in-place rent will hold with a different tenant.

faqs.q: Does a single-specialty build-out hurt a medical office building's exchange value?
faqs.a: It can, because a highly specific build-out narrows the pool of tenants who could step into that suite without another round of tenant improvements. That narrower pool should show up as a wider cap rate or a discount against comparable general-practice space, not get priced the same.

faqs.q: Why is medical office space competing with life-science lab space near Torrey Pines and UTC?
faqs.a: Landlords in that corridor can often convert standard office floor plates to lab-capable space, and some are weighing that conversion against continuing medical office use in the same building. That competition affects pricing and availability even for buildings that stay medical office.

faqs.q: How much parking does a medical office replacement property need in San Diego?
faqs.a: Medical uses generally require a higher parking ratio than standard office because of patient turnover throughout the day, and cities set that ratio in the zoning code rather than leaving it to the landlord. Check the site's actual ratio against the code requirement for medical occupancy before assuming the existing count is compliant.

faqs.q: How does San Diego's thin medical office inventory affect the 45-day identification window?
faqs.a: Because medical office listings don't turn over quickly, waiting to start the search until partway through the identification window leaves fewer real candidates to choose from. Building the short list before the relinquished property even closes gives the qualified intermediary more workable options inside the 45-day rule.
